disease_label_per_paper: HSV-2 encephalitis complicated by delayed temporal lobe hemorrhage after acyclovir initiation
presentation_summary: 40-year-old left-handed Caucasian woman with chronic headaches and 20-pack-year smoking history presented with one week of diffuse generalized headache, fever, nausea, emesis, and photophobia.
Initial cranial imaging was negative for hemorrhage and physical examination had no focal neurologic deficit.
CSF showed 558 WBC/mm3 with 100% monocytes, protein 115 mg/dL, and glucose 55 mg/dL.
CSF PCR was positive for HSV-2, establishing HSV-2 encephalitis.
Acyclovir was initiated; one week later she developed acute altered mental status and left-sided weakness.
Cranial imaging showed a large right temporal lobe hemorrhage with significant midline shift; CTA showed no vascular lesion.
She underwent right hemicraniectomy and temporal lobectomy, completed three weeks of acyclovir, and was discharged to acute rehabilitation.
